draft.title: Conditional probability
card: \(\text{Pr}(A \mid B)\) is the probability of \(A\) given that \(B\) has happened. Knowing \(B\) has happened shrinks the sample space to just the outcomes in \(B\).
Formula: \(\text{Pr}(A \mid B) = \frac{\text{Pr}(A \cap B)}{\text{Pr}(B)}\). The bottom is the event we are given. The top is the part of it that is also \(A\).
Example: roll a die. Given the roll is even, the outcomes left are 2, 4 and 6. So \(\text{Pr}(6 \mid \text{even}) = \frac{1}{3}\). The total is 3, not 6.
draft.remember: Given \(B\) means \(B\) is the new total. Divide by \(\text{Pr}(B)\), not by everything.

a.q: Events \(A\) and \(B\) have \(\text{Pr}(A \cap B) = 0.2\) and \(\text{Pr}(B) = 0.5\). What is \(\text{Pr}(A \mid B)\)?
a.why: \(\text{Pr}(A \mid B) = \text{Pr}(A \cap B) \div \text{Pr}(B)\), which is \(0.2 \div 0.5 = 0.4\). Multiplying gives 0.1, but the formula divides by the probability of the given event.
a.clue: The event after the bar goes on the bottom.

b.q: On a camp, 40 students picked activities. Of the 25 who chose kayaking, 10 also chose archery. Another 5 chose archery only. A student who chose archery is picked at random. What is the probability they also chose kayaking?
b.why: Archery has \(10 + 5 = 15\) students, and 10 of them chose kayaking, so the probability is \(\frac{10}{15} = \frac{2}{3}\). The option \(\frac{2}{5}\) is \(\frac{10}{25}\), which divides by the kayakers and so reverses the condition. The given event is archery, so it goes on the bottom.
b.clue: Find the total number who chose archery first.

proposal.title: Conditional probability

Formula: \(\text{Pr}(A \mid B) = \frac{\text{Pr}(A \cap B)}{\text{Pr}(B)}\). The bottom is the event we are given. The top is the part of it that is also \(A\).
